steps.title: Good News
steps.body: Unseen poetry tests skills, not knowledge. You can't revise the poems, so focus on developing analysis techniques.

steps.title: Form Significance
steps.body: Why did the poet choose this form? A sonnet about love connects to tradition. Free verse about trauma suggests breaking from conventions.

steps.title: Top Tip
steps.body: For unseen poetry, the 24-mark analysis question gets roughly 30 minutes and the 8-mark comparison gets 10-15 minutes. Always spend 5 minutes reading and annotating before writing anything — a well-planned 25-minute answer will always outperform a rushed 30-minute one.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: What should you do in your first reading of an unseen poem? | Why is it important to identify the form of the poem? | What's the difference between basic and developed interpretation?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: First reading: understand meaning - what's happening, who's speaking, what's the mood. Don't analyse yet - just comprehend the poem's basic content. | Identifying form helps you understand context and intent. A sonnet suggests love/serious topic; free verse suggests modern/conversational approach. | Basic: identifies what (e.g., "the poem is about loss"). Developed: explains why and how (e.g., "the poem explores how loss echoes through memory").
